knitr::opts_chunk$set(

In this vignette, we show the hourly PM2.5 of 2023 at two CPCB stations: Powai
in Mumbai, and Silk Board, a busy traffic junction in Bengaluru. We use
`plot_aqi_radial_hourly()`, which draws each hour on a 24-hour clock in IST.

## Download the data

We download the raw 15-minute values with `cpcb_raw_readings()`. CPCB times are
in IST.

```{r cached, include=FALSE}
raw_file <- here::here("vignettes/data/diurnal/raw_pm25_2023.csv")
cached <- file.exists(raw_file)
if (cached) {
  raw <- read.csv(raw_file)
  raw$timestamp <- as.POSIXct(raw$timestamp, tz = "UTC", format = "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S")
}
```

```{r download, eval = !cached}
raw <- cpcb_raw_readings(c("site_5112", "site_1558"), 2023, "PM2.5")
```

```{r stations}
table(raw$station_name)
```

## Calculate the hourly sub-index

We take the mean of each hour and convert it to the CPCB PM2.5 sub-index with
`aqi_sub_index()`. CPCB defines the sub-index for a 24-hour mean, so the hourly
value is not an official AQI. It puts each hour on the AQI category scale.

```{r hourly}
raw$hour <- as.POSIXct(format(raw$timestamp, "%Y-%m-%d %H:00:00"), tz = "UTC")
hourly <- aggregate(value ~ station_name + hour, raw, mean)
hourly$value <- aqi_sub_index("PM2.5", hourly$value)
hourly$city <- sub(" - .*", "", hourly$station_name)
names(hourly)[names(hourly) == "hour"] <- "timestamp"
head(hourly)
```

## Show the daily cycle in each month

By default, each ring is a month, with January at the centre and midnight at the
top.

```{r clock}
plot_aqi_radial_hourly(hourly)
```

Powai is cleanest from May to September, when every hour is Good. In winter it
peaks at 09:00 to 10:00, when morning traffic adds to the shallow night-time air
layer; in January, 06:00 to 12:00 is Poor. Silk Board changes less with the
season and is Good at every hour only in June and July. Its winter day has two
peaks, 64 to 65 µg/m³ at 07:00 to 08:00 and 61 µg/m³ at 20:00, against 34 µg/m³
at 14:00 to 15:00. The peaks match the morning and evening traffic at the
junction.

## Show one ring for each day

Set `rings = "day"` for one ring per date. Short events become visible, such as
Diwali on 12 November 2023.

```{r days, fig.height = 7}
plot_aqi_radial_hourly(hourly, rings = "day")
```

At both stations, the night-time PM2.5 rose from 21 to 50 µg/m³ on 8 to 10
November to 104 to 152 µg/m³ on 12 and 13 November.
